cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
cards.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. These minutes say 'discussion of my proposal.' What did you leave out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sign them and we can eat. Nobody wanted an awkward record.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. 'Nobody' sounds crowded. Who wanted my name out of it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. I suggested someone else present, to save your proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who else? You've recorded my rescue very carefully without naming my replacement.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims control and A3 presses who, but A5 questioning does not explicitly use the requested signature as a continuing approval condition beyond stock status text.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 nobody/no awkward record prompts A3 who query; B4 self-admission plus someone else prompts A5 missing name, a coherent incomplete-answer chain.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the record signed and dinner started; B4 admits a protective intervention, plausible reasons for careful wording.

heightening.evidence: B4 reveals a rescue but leaves presenter unnamed, giving A5 a specific remaining omission to pursue.

specificity.evidence: A1 minutes/proposal and B2 signature establish review context; B4 states that A would be replaced as presenter.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 carefully unnamed rescue is pointed, while the generic decision prefix adds little to the actual gate.
